_description: Validates cross-operator federation: the Open Trust Evaluation over an operator's published signed protocol metadata and conformance evidence, operator discovery, routing, execution, obligations, events, settlement, and failure modes.

sub_suites.name: Signed Protocol Metadata Validation
sub_suites.description: An operator's published signed protocol metadata is accepted only when it is not expired, its signature resolves to the trust root or a delegated signing key in the active Key Manifest, its signing key_id is listed there, and the accompanying conformance evidence is valid.

cases.title: Valid signed protocol metadata accepted
cases.description: Signed protocol metadata whose signature resolves to a key in the active Key Manifest, with an active issuer_key_id and a future expiry, must be accepted.

cases.title: Expired signed protocol metadata rejected
Signed protocol metadata with an invalid signature rejected
Unknown signing key rejected
cases.description: Signed protocol metadata whose signing key_id is not listed in the active Key Manifest must be rejected.

cases.title: Mismatched operator_id rejected
L2 conformance scope cannot access L3 federation
cases.description: An operator whose published conformance evidence covers only conformance scope L2 cannot participate in L3 federation flows.

cases.title: Metadata without routing capability cannot federate
Signed protocol metadata must be at canonical path
cases.description: The operator's signed protocol metadata must be resolvable at /.well-known/banza/signed-protocol-metadata.json on the operator's declared domain.

cases.title: Revoked operator (in BRL) rejected
cases.description: Structurally valid signed protocol metadata is rejected when the operator appears in the current BRL, regardless of any other trust signal. The SPM here is operator-b-test (SPM-B-VALID), the operator that BRL-REVOKED-PEER revokes — so the composed vector actually exercises operator_revoked_in_brl. (Corrected from SPM-A-VALID, whose operator-a-test was not the revoked operator, so the pairing could not produce the declared verdict.)

cases.title: Re-published trust material preserves operator identity
cases.description: When an operator re-publishes its signed protocol metadata and conformance evidence before expiry, the operator_id and public key must remain the same. A change of operator_id on re-publication is a protocol violation.

sub_suites.name: Operator Discovery
sub_suites.description: Operator discovery validates manifest resolution, federation capability declaration, and manifest integrity.

cases.title: Valid manifest resolved for federation
cases.description: A manifest with supports_federation:true and a valid signed_protocol_metadata_url is accepted for L3 routing.

cases.title: Manifest without federation flag not routable
Manifest capability mismatch rejected
Manifest with unsupported protocol version rejected
Manifest with wrong operator_id rejected
Manifest B without federation identified correctly
cases.description: An operator-B manifest without federation support must not receive routed payments.

cases.title: Manifest declaring federation without published conformance evidence rejected
cases.description: Declaring supports_federation:true without published L3+ conformance evidence is a protocol violation: supports_federation requires published L3+ conformance evidence (INV-FEDEVAL-007).

sub_suites.name: Open Trust Evaluation
sub_suites.description: The Open Trust Evaluation (ADR-025) is ten conjunctive, fail-closed checks a routing peer runs locally over the evaluated operator's published material: signatures resolve to the trust root or a delegated signing key in the active Key Manifest, trust material is fresh, and nothing involved is revoked. Any missing, invalid, expired, revoked, or incompatible material fails the evaluation closed.

cases.title: Valid key manifest accepted
Key manifest with missing issuer key rejected
Empty BRL means no active revocations
Revoked peer in BRL rejected
Stale BRL triggers re-fetch before routing
cases.description: A BRL older than the staleness threshold must be re-fetched before any routing decision.

cases.title: Emergency BRL update processed without delay
cases.description: Emergency revocations must be applied within 60 minutes per §14.9.

cases.title: Signature resolves from trust root through a delegated key to the operator's metadata
cases.description: Each step from the trust root, through a delegated signing key in the active Key Manifest, to the operator's signed protocol metadata must be cryptographically verifiable. Any gap in the chain invalidates the terminal signature.

cases.title: Revoking a delegated signing key invalidates every signature made under it
cases.description: If a delegated signing key is revoked via the trust root, all signed protocol metadata and conformance evidence signed under that key become invalid regardless of their individual expiry.

cases.title: BRL must be re-verified at each routing decision
cases.description: Caching the BRL result beyond the staleness window and using it for routing is a protocol violation.

sub_suites.name: Federation Routing
sub_suites.description: Cross-operator routing decisions must follow the routing contract. Invalid routing requests must be rejected deterministically.

cases.title: Valid routing request accepted
Unknown recipient rejected
Suspended recipient rejected
Wrong currency rejected
Wrong destination operator rejected
Zero amount rejected
Duplicate routing request with different content rejected
cases.description: Same idempotency_key with different payload content must return 409 Conflict.

cases.title: Accepted routing response processed correctly
Rejected routing response handled without fund loss
cases.description: A rejection response from the destination operator must result in no ledger entries at the source.

sub_suites.name: Cross-Operator Execution
sub_suites.description: Cross-operator payment execution must preserve double-entry integrity, idempotency, and atomicity across the operator boundary.

cases.title: Cross-operator payment executes when the Open Trust Evaluation passes
Idempotent re-submission returns original result
cases.description: A duplicate routing request with the same idempotency_key and same content must return the original accepted result without creating a duplicate transfer.

cases.title: Idempotency conflict on same key, different content
Source operator deducts balance before routing
cases.description: The source operator must debit the sender wallet before emitting the routing request. If routing fails, the debit is reversed.

cases.title: Destination operator credits balance on receipt
cases.description: The destination operator must credit the recipient wallet upon receiving a valid routing request. The credit must be reflected in the ledger.

cases.title: Both operators emit events on cross-operator transfer
Rejected routing response triggers source-side rollback
Timeout during routing triggers safe abort
cases.description: If the destination operator does not respond within the routing timeout window, the source operator must abort and reverse the debit.

cases.title: Double-entry maintained across operator boundary
cases.description: The sum of DEBIT entries at the source plus the sum of CREDIT entries at the destination must equal zero when summed across both ledgers for the same cross-operator transfer.

cases.title: Transfer amount immutable once routing accepted
cases.description: After the destination operator accepts the routing request, the amount_minor cannot be modified. Any attempt to alter the amount is a protocol violation.

sub_suites.name: Federation Obligations
sub_suites.description: Each operator participating in federation carries enforceable obligations. Sustained, unresolved breach is grounds for revoking the operator's trust material.

cases.title: Receiving operator must credit within obligation window
cases.description: The destination operator must credit the recipient wallet within the obligation window defined in federation-obligation.json.

cases.title: Receiving operator must emit payment.received event
Receiving operator must confirm receipt to routing operator
cases.description: The destination operator must return an accepted routing response before the obligation timeout.

cases.title: Sending operator must include trace_id on routed payment
cases.description: All cross-operator routing requests must include a trace_id conforming to the tr-{uuid} format.

cases.title: Operator must verify BRL before accepting routed payment
cases.description: Before crediting on a routed payment, the destination operator must verify the source operator is not in the current BRL.

cases.title: Obligation timeout triggers federation incident
cases.description: If a destination operator fails to confirm receipt within the obligation window, the incident is logged and sustained failures are grounds for revocation.

cases.title: Operators must support idempotent receipt
cases.description: A destination operator must accept re-delivery of a routing request with the same idempotency_key without creating a duplicate credit.

cases.title: Repeated obligation breach is grounds for revocation
cases.description: Three or more unresolved obligation breaches within a 30-day window are grounds for revoking the operator's trust material per §12.

sub_suites.name: Federation Events
sub_suites.description: Federation events must conform to the event envelope schema and carry correct trace and correlation identifiers across operator boundaries.

cases.title: Cross-operator payment emits payment.sent at source
Cross-operator payment emits payment.received at destination
Federation routing event includes routing_operator_id
cases.description: Events emitted for cross-operator transfers must include the routing_operator_id in the payload.

cases.title: Events carry matching trace_id across operator boundary
cases.description: The trace_id on payment.sent at the source must equal the trace_id on payment.received at the destination.

cases.title: Events use operator-scoped correlation_id
cases.description: Each operator's events carry that operator's own correlation_id. The cross-operator trace_id provides the linking mechanism.

cases.title: payment.sent emitted before payment.received
cases.description: In any cross-operator transfer, payment.sent (source) must have a created_at timestamp earlier than payment.received (destination).

cases.title: Retry of routed payment must not produce duplicate events
cases.description: An idempotent re-submission must not emit a second payment.sent or payment.received event.

cases.title: Federation event schema matches federation-event.json contract

sub_suites.name: Cross-Operator Settlement
sub_suites.description: Settlement of cross-operator transfers must be idempotent, complete, and reconcilable against ledger entries.

cases.title: Cross-operator transfers appear in source operator settlement batch
cases.description: Each cross-operator payment initiated by an operator must appear in that operator's settlement batch.

cases.title: Settlement batch amount matches sum of cross-operator transfers
cases.description: The gross_minor in the settlement batch must equal the sum of all amount_minor values of the included transfers.

cases.title: Net settlement = gross minus fees
cases.description: net_minor in settlement batch must equal gross_minor minus any applicable federation fees.

cases.title: Settlement re-submission with same batch_id is idempotent
cases.description: Re-submitting a settlement batch with the same batch_id must return the original result without creating a duplicate settlement.

cases.title: Each transfer appears in exactly one settlement batch
settlement.completed event emitted after batch confirmation
Failed settlement triggers reconciliation process
cases.description: If a settlement batch fails, the operator must initiate reconciliation per §13.4 and must not mark transfers as settled.

cases.title: Settlement obligation schema matches federation-obligation.json
Partial settlement not permitted
cases.description: A settlement batch must either be fully applied or fully rejected. Partial application is a protocol violation.

sub_suites.name: Federation Failure Modes
sub_suites.description: Protocol invariants must be maintained under failure conditions. No single failure must result in fund loss or double-spend.

cases.title: Routing operator unavailable — payment not initiated
cases.description: If the routing intermediary is unavailable, the source operator must not initiate the transfer. No ledger entries must be created.

cases.title: Destination operator unavailable — routing fails gracefully
cases.description: Unavailability of destination must result in a clean rejected response, not a hung transaction.

cases.title: Trust-material expiry during routing results in clean rejection
cases.description: If the operator's signed protocol metadata expires between routing request and response, the payment must be rejected cleanly. The source debit must be reversed.

cases.title: BRL unavailability uses cached BRL with staleness flag
cases.description: If BRL endpoint is unreachable, the last known BRL may be used within the staleness window. Beyond the window, routing must be suspended.

cases.title: Network partition does not result in double-spend
cases.description: If a network partition occurs between the routing request being sent and the response received, the source operator must use idempotency semantics to prevent double creation.

cases.title: Double routing prevented by idempotency
cases.description: Two concurrent routing requests with the same idempotency_key must result in exactly one transfer.

cases.title: Destination failure during receipt does not leave funds in limbo
cases.description: If the destination operator crashes after debiting but before confirming, the source operator's reversal mechanism must reclaim the funds.

cases.title: All protocol invariants maintained under failure scenarios
cases.description: Failure scenarios must not cause invariant violations. Verification is performed by checking ledger state after each failure injection.
